answer: Divergent checkpoint lottery: at each dawn interval, every identity must answer a random challenge from its private interaction log and sign it with a secure-element key. A quill challenge forces the agent to reveal one fresh log-derived bit; two identities returning the same bit are clones and lose their prepaid compute credit. Any ripple of identical answers across a batch invalidates all registrations, so an attacker must buy separate secure elements and maintain distinct logs per identity.
